newsitem.title: USA: US Plains feedlot cattle not well tested - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains feedlot cattle not well tested - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sales Tuesday were slow, with not enough sold for an adequate market test, feedlot sources and USDA said.

About 200 head of slaughter steers and heifers that will likely grade mostly select, with a few choice, sold in Kansas at $64.00 per cwt, USDA said. There were no reported sales in the Texas Panhandle, feedlot sources said.

The bulk of this week's showlist continued to be priced at $66.00 to $67.00 amid light packer bids at $64.00, sources said. Feedlot cattle prices this week were seen steady with last week at $65.00, but could turn lower on weak beef prices.
Beef prices at midday were quoted down $0.09 to $1.09 per cwt on 193 fabricated loads sold, USDA said.
Sliding beef prices were eroding packer operating margins and curbing packers' interest in bidding any higher than $64.00, sources said.

However, several feedlot managers said owners still expected at least steady prices at $65.00. Their optimism was linked to ideas several packers were short on supplies and would need to buy cattle before the end of the week for quick shipment, sources said.
